reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - plasma concentration 7638 ng/ml and intra-tumoral level 3270 ng/ml demonstrate adequate drug exposure and tissue penetration. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear evidence of pathway modulation - CD133+ neurospheres reduced from 11% to 3%, and Sonic Hedgehog pathway activation was measured by RT-PCR and IHC, confirming the target was engaged and the intended mechanism was activated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite confirmed target engagement and pathway modulation, the primary endpoint failed - 6-month PFS was 0% in the vismodegib arm vs 5% in control. Both PFS and OS endpoints showed failure outcomes. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No meaningful subgroup response - progressive disease occurred in 13/17 vismodegib patients vs 11/16 controls, showing no benefit. Stable disease was achieved in 4/17 vs 5/16, again showing no advantage. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues - adequate sample size for a Phase 2 trial, appropriate duration, no manufacturing issues reported. This represents a clear case where the mechanism was engaged but did not translate to clinical benefit.
